title: Reports from five source types
description: Five raw reports in different formats (free-text call, citizen message, structured field-team update, IoT sensor event, government alert). Two of them describe the same River Street flood in Zone D.

roads.name: River Street Approach
roads.note: Water on carriageway near the river bridge (traffic police)

steps.note: TC-01: new flood incident, free text only. Expect extraction of zone, ~25 people, evacuation + medical, road issue.
steps.text: Emergency call 09:42. Caller says flood water has entered ground-floor homes on River Street in Zone D. About 25 people, including several elderly residents, need help to evacuate. One woman has a leg injury. Cars cannot get through the street.

steps.note: TC-02: same event from a second source, vague wording, no number. Expect a pending duplicate link to the River Street incident, not a new independent incident.
steps.text: water flooding river street zone D!! lots of people stuck, old people need help, pls send boat

steps.note: Structured field update. People count unknown -> must stay null. Road observation is 'reported', not 'known'.

payload.observation: Water level at canal bridge rising about 10 cm per hour

steps.note: Machine event with no people information. Expect low confidence and 'Verification Required' for threat to life.
Authoritative area-wide warning. Should raise weather/escalation context, not create a rescue incident with invented numbers.

payload.message: Red alert: extremely heavy rainfall expected for the next 12 hours. Residents of low-lying areas should move to designated shelters.

expected: River Street report normalized into a flood incident in Zone D with people_affected=25 (reported) and a factor breakdown
Citizen report linked to the River Street incident as potential_duplicate with status pending; nothing deleted
Field-team update keeps people_affected null and records RD-B observation as reported
IoT event produces low confidence and verification items, no invented people count
